in_hebrew.meaning: dome, vault, hut, pen, fold, enclosure, stable
in_hebrew.long_meaning: A place of shelter, protection, or confinement. Can be a physical structure such as a hut or a pen, or a metaphorical one such as a 'fold' for sheep.

in_greek.name: χαμηλ

data.cultural_impact: The name Hammel holds significance in the Christian faith due to its connection with the Parable of the Good Shepherd. In this parable, Jesus describes himself as the good shepherd who lays down his life for his sheep. Hammel, as a name derived from the Greek word hammon or 'reverence', carries the echoes of this doctrine in its etymology. Historically, the name Hammel may have also been associated with the traditional role of shepherds in raising and caring for livestock, connecting it to the agrarian roots of ancient communities.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hammel holds deep spiritual significance as a reminder of the selfless love and care embodied in the Parable of the Good Shepherd. As a spiritual name, Hammel calls to mind the protective, nurturing role that God plays in our lives, watching over us and guiding us in the same way that a good shepherd watches over his flock. This name serves as a reminder of the divine reverence due to the Creator and the tender, loving care He extends to his children.

historical_references.reference: The name Hammel has been used throughout Christian history by saints, scholars, and faithful believers who exemplified its meaning.
